The petitioners seek grant of bail for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short).

2. Heard the arguments of Sri. Gangadhar K., learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt. N. Anitha NC: 2023:KHC:37717 Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State.
3.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that, the first petitioner is not a resident of Bengaluru, she resides in Tamil Nadu.
Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the sisters and brother-in-law of accused No.1.
For the reason of the accused No.1 married to the deceased, they gave their house in the third floor.
Petitioners have not involved in the matrimonial affairs of accused No.1 and the deceased.
Accused No.1 was not absconded and he was readily available at the spot and he has already been arrested and interrogated.
For the reason of petitioners being the mother, sister and brother- in-law, they have arraigned as accused persons.
At the time of deceased fell down from the third floor of the building, none of these petitioners were present.
There is no specific allegation that the petitioners have involved either subjecting the deceased to cruelty or abetted for commission of any alleged offences.
They are ready to NC: 2023:KHC:37717 assist for investigation and abide by any conditions that would be imposed.

4. Per contra, learned HCGP has contended that the marriage between the accused No.1 with the deceased was performed on 06.04.2022 and the alleged incident took place on 23.09.2023 within one and half years of the marriage.

The allegation is that the deceased was subjected to cruelty,
harassment in demand of dowry, she was driven out of house; she was brought back one week prior to the alleged incident to the matrimonial home.

sentences.text: They are required for custodial interrogation, if bail is granted, they will flee away from justice and sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and perused the records.
6. The materials on record point out that the marriage between the accused No.1 with deceased - Ramya R. was performed on 06.04.2022.
The deceased NC: 2023:KHC:37717 and their parents hail from Cuddalore District, Tamil Nadu.

It is alleged that at that at the time of marriage, demand of dowry in the form of gold, silver, furniture was given to accused No.1 thereafter, accused No.1 brought the deceased and took the house in the third floor from accused No.2 on lease for a sum of Rs.5 lakhs and resided therein.
The accused No.1 had an illicit relationship with some lady, in this regard, there was a quarrel between him and the deceased.
In the meantime, the deceased become pregnant and gave birth to a child, she was sent to parental home for confinement and she was returned to matrimonial home.
The parents of the deceased advised the accused No.1 while sending the deceased back to the matrimonial home that he would disown his bad vices and to lead happy matrimonial life.
On 23.09.2023, the deceased had a phone call communication with his mother.
On the very next day morning at 7.00 a.m., she received a phone call from accused No.2 that the deceased was died having fell down from the building.
The parents NC: 2023:KHC:37717 of the deceased came down to Bengaluru and set the law into motion.

7. On careful perusal of the complaint averments it is seen that there is no specific allegations against these petitioners that before marriage, they have demanded any dowry, post-marriage, they have involved in subjecting the deceased to harassment for the purpose of dowry.
There is no allegation that petitioners were present when the alleged incident took place and they were the cause for the death of the deceased.
Learned Sessions Judge for the reason that it is the case of dowry death declined to exercise discretion.
8. Having considered the materials on record, there is no material which would point out towards the petitioners, which prima facie attract the alleged offences against them.
Matter under investigation.
Accused No.1
has already arrested and interrogated, the petitioners undertaken to abide any terms and conditions that would be imposed.
Hence, there is no reason to refuse exercise of discretion in favour of the petitioners.
Hence, the NC: 2023:KHC:37717 petition deserves merit consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The Petition is allowed.
(ii) The petitioners are ordered to be released on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.338/2023 of Jnanabharathi Police, Bengaluru City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of IPC, on execution of a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-
